text: Along f:A→B, an A-linear endomorphism φ extends by b⊗m↦b·(f⊗id)(φ(1⊗m)). This is the [scalar-extension universal property, Stacks 10.14.3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3). The source constructs the unique B-linear map with this formula over semirings, allowing noncommutative A but requiring commutative B; no injectivity, flatness or basis is assumed. Checks pass: [mapValue_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L114), [eq_mapValue](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L141).
Checks the defining formula on pure tensors.
Checks uniqueness from the comparison square.

The extended map sends b⊗m to b times the comparison image of φ(1⊗m). Thus its values are determined on the B-generators 1⊗m, in accord with [Stacks 10.14.3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3). The comparison need not embed A⊗M in B⊗M; the formula is a linear extension, not an inverse-map construction. Checks pass: [mapValue_comp_rTensor](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L120), [mapValue_one](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L155).
Checks the full comparison square.
Checks that the formula sends identity to identity.

The comparison j=f⊗id intertwines φ with its extension: φ_B∘j=j∘φ. The source proves this on pure tensors using A-linearity of φ and semilinearity of j. It is the square characterizing [scalar extension](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3), stated over the common base R; neither composite requires j to be injective. Checks pass: [mapValue_rTensor_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L133), [eq_mapValue](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L141).
Checks the square on every tensor.
Checks that this square uniquely determines the extension.

For every z∈A⊗M, applying the extended endomorphism to j(z) equals j(φ(z)). This is the elementwise form of the [scalar-extension comparison square](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3). It applies to arbitrary tensors, not only pure ones, and follows by evaluating the already proved equality of R-linear composites. Checks pass: [mapValue_comp_rTensor](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L120), [mapValue_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L114).
Provides the full equality of linear composites.
Checks the underlying extension on pure tensors.

The comparison square determines a B-linear endomorphism uniquely because j(1⊗m)=1⊗m and these elements generate B⊗M over B. This is the uniqueness in [Stacks 10.14.3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3). Surjectivity of j as an R-linear map is unnecessary; the source compares the corresponding maps from M under scalar-extension adjunction. Checks pass: [mapValue_comp_rTensor](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L120), [mapValue_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L114).
The constructed extension satisfies the required square.
Checks the values forced on B-generators.

The identity endomorphism extends to the identity: both satisfy the same comparison square, so uniqueness identifies them. This is preservation of identity by [scalar extension](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3). Here 1 denotes the identity map in the endomorphism semiring, rather than a constant map taking every vector to a unit. Checks pass: [mapValue_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L114), [mapValue_id](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L271).
Checks identity extension on generating tensors.
Separately checks extension along the identity algebra map.

Extending φψ equals composing the two extended maps. Multiplication in an endomorphism semiring means composition, so ψ acts first and φ second. Substituting their comparison squares proves multiplicativity by [scalar-extension uniqueness](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3); no commutativity of φ and ψ, or of the source algebra A, is required. Checks pass: [mapValue_comp_rTensor](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L120), [mapValueGL_coe](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L207).
Checks the square used for each composite.
Checks the same operation under the induced map on invertible endomorphisms.

The zero endomorphism extends to zero because every generator 1⊗m is sent to zero, and extension is B-linear. This agrees with the [linear scalar-extension construction](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3). The source instead uses its equivalent uniqueness characterization; zero modules and zero value algebras are included without additional hypotheses. Checks pass: [mapValue_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L114), [mapValue_add](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L177).
Checks the defining formula on generators.
Checks compatibility with the additive operation containing zero.

Scalar extension preserves pointwise addition of endomorphisms: (φ+ψ)_B=φ_B+ψ_B. The comparison map and both extensions are additive, so the sum satisfies the required square; uniqueness finishes the proof. This is the additive behavior of the [extension adjunction](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3), valid for semimodules without assuming additive inverses. Checks pass: [mapValue_comp_rTensor](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L120), [mapValueRingHom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L195).
Checks the comparison square used to identify the sum.
Checks that the packaged homomorphism has this underlying map.

This packages extension of endomorphisms as a homomorphism preserving addition, multiplication, zero and one, using the proved comparison-square laws. It agrees with [scalar extension](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3). Lean calls the type RingHom even for semirings; here no additive inverses are assumed, and multiplication remains ordered composition of endomorphisms. Checks pass: [mapValue_add](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L177), [mapValue_mul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L161), [mapValue_one](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L155).
Checks addition preservation.
Checks ordered composition preservation.
Checks preservation of the identity map.

The packaged endomorphism homomorphism evaluates to the previously defined scalar-extension map itself. This confirms that packaging the operation laws does not change the map supplied by the [extension universal property](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3). The equality is definitional; RingHom is used for semirings as well, without asserting additive inverses. Checks pass: [mapValue_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L114), [mapValue_mul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L161).
Computes the underlying map on pure tensors.
Checks the multiplication law carried by the package.

Applying the endomorphism homomorphism to units gives the group homomorphism on invertible linear maps. The extension of an inverse is inverse to the extension because multiplication and identity are preserved. This realizes base change of [Milne’s Aut_V functor](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=112); no determinant, basis or finite-dimensionality is used. Checks pass: [mapValueGL_coe](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L207), [mapValue_mul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L161), [mapValue_one](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L155).
Checks the underlying endomorphism of the extended unit.
Checks multiplication, which transports both inverse identities.
Checks the identity appearing in the inverse identities.

Forgetting the inverse from an extended automorphism gives exactly the extended underlying endomorphism. The source applies Units.map to the endomorphism homomorphism, so this equation exposes its actual value. It matches the [scalar-extension action on Aut_V](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=112), with units meaning invertible operators rather than invertible scalars. Checks pass: [mapValue_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L114), [mapValue_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L215).
Checks that value on every pure tensor.
Checks compatibility with successive changes of value algebra.

Extension along A→B→C equals successive extension first to B and then to C. Both maps satisfy the square for the composite comparison, so [scalar-extension uniqueness](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3) identifies them. The source permits noncommutative A, while B and C are commutative; the displayed order agrees with ordinary composition. Checks pass: [mapValue_rTensor_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L133), [mapValue_id](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L271).
Checks compatibility with each comparison map.
Checks the identity case of the functorial law.

Extending an endomorphism along the identity algebra homomorphism leaves it unchanged. The comparison f⊗id is identity, so the original endomorphism satisfies the defining square. This is the identity law for [scalar extension](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05G3); this declaration lies in the commutative-source-algebra section, matching its elaborated hypotheses. Checks pass: [mapValue_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L114), [mapValue_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L215).
Checks the identity specialization on pure tensors.
Checks the corresponding composition law.

At A, the group-valued functor is exactly Aut_A(A⊗V), encoded by invertible endomorphisms. This is [Milne VIII§2’s Aut_V(A)](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=112), with scalar factors first. The source exposes the functor’s chosen object by equality; it imposes neither a basis on V nor representability of this functor by a scheme. Checks pass: [val_mapScalarExtensionAutomorphisms](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/ScalarExtension.lean#L128), [scalarExtensionAutomorphismsFunctor_map](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/ScalarExtension.lean#L226).
Checks the underlying maps between these concrete groups.
Checks the matching identification on morphisms.

The functor sends φ:A→B to extension of automorphisms, surrounded by the equality identifications of its source and target groups. This is the morphism assignment of [Milne’s Aut_V functor](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf#page=112). Those identifications change only packaging; the scalar-extension operator is unchanged and is not assumed injective. Checks pass: [mapScalarExtensionAutomorphisms_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/ScalarExtension.lean#L138), [mapScalarExtensionAutomorphisms_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/ScalarExtension.lean#L195).
Checks the operator on pure tensors.
Checks covariance under composition of algebra maps.

The comparison j=f⊗id satisfies j(a·z)=f(a)·j(z). This is semilinearity, obtained from f(ab)=f(a)f(b) on pure tensors and then additivity. It agrees with the [tensor universal property](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV); the source proves it for semirings, allowing both value algebras to be noncommutative while the base is commutative. Checks pass: [scalarExtensionMap_smul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/ScalarExtension.lean#L110), [mapValue_comp_rTensor](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/End/ScalarExtension.lean#L120).
Checks the concrete value-algebra comparison in the commutative-ring specialization.
Uses this semilinearity in the full extension square.

In a compatible tower R→A→B, tensoring the A-linear structure map A→B and tensoring its underlying R-algebra map give the same function A⊗M→B⊗M. The source identifies both as a↦algebraMap(a) on the scalar leg, matching the [tensor construction](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV). Their packaged linearity differs, so equality is stated on values. Checks pass: [rTensor_toLinearMap_apply_smul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Tower.lean#L34), [scalarExtensionMap_eq_map](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/ScalarExtension.lean#L78).
Checks semilinearity of the underlying algebra-map construction.
Checks the concrete comparison is the corresponding tensor map in its ring specialization.

The equivalence sends n⊗((b⊗p)⊗(c⊗q)) to (bc)·n⊗(p⊗q). It combines distribution of scalar extension with [tensor associativity and the unit law](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV), absorbing both B-coefficients into N. The inverse inserts two units. Compatible R- and B-actions are required; this is a B-linear isomorphism without flatness assumptions. Checks pass: [cancelBaseChangeTensor_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/ScalarExtension.lean#L151), [cancelBaseChangeTensor_symm_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/ScalarExtension.lean#L158).
Checks the actual product of the two coefficients.
Checks the inverse inserts both unit coefficients.

On the displayed nested pure tensor, cancellation multiplies b and c and applies bc to n, leaving p⊗q in order. This follows from the explicit distribution and cancellation equivalences behind [tensor associativity](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV). B is commutative and its action on N is compatible with R; no tensor factors are discarded. Checks pass: [cancelBaseChangeTensor_symm_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/ScalarExtension.lean#L158), [cancelBaseChangeTensor_tmul_distribBaseChange](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/ScalarExtension.lean#L165).
Checks the inverse formula on pure tensors.
Checks cancellation after the full distribution comparison.

After distributing b⊗z across the two scalar-extended factors, cancellation yields (b·n)⊗z. This is the compatibility of the two chosen [tensor identifications](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV), with z an arbitrary tensor in P⊗Q. The scalar is absorbed into N, and the formula does not presume that z is pure. Checks pass: [cancelBaseChangeTensor_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/ScalarExtension.lean#L151), [cancelBaseChangeTensor_symm_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/ScalarExtension.lean#L158).
Checks the constituent formula on generating tensors.
Checks the inverse coefficient insertion.

Cancelling N⊗_B(B⊗P) to N⊗_R P commutes with applying a B-linear map f to N. On n⊗(b⊗p), both sides become f(bn)⊗p=b·f(n)⊗p. This is naturality of [tensor associativity and scalar collapse](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV); restricting scalars changes the recorded linearity of f, not its function. Checks pass: [restrictScalars_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/RestrictScalars.lean#L148).
Checks the concrete comodule-morphism consumer built using this cancellation square.

This identifies M with the R-linear image of m↦1⊗m. FaithfulSMul makes R→K injective; Module.Flat means tensoring with M preserves injections (over semirings, mono-flatness). Thus the unit-tensor map is injective, as in the ring criterion [Stacks 10.39.5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00H9). The codomain is its image, not all K⊗M. Checks pass: [coe_unitTmulEquiv_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/ScalarExtension.lean#L243), [unitTmulEquiv_symm_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/ScalarExtension.lean#L250).
Checks the forward map is the actual unit tensor.
Checks recovery from the unit tensor in its image.

The equivalence onto the unit-tensor image sends m to exactly 1⊗m in K⊗M. Its hypotheses are faithful scalar action and preservation of injections by tensoring with M—the semiring meaning of Module.Flat, agreeing with [ordinary ring flatness](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00H9). The equality describes the canonical inclusion of the image, without claiming surjectivity onto K⊗M. Checks pass: [unitTmulEquiv_symm_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/ScalarExtension.lean#L250).
Checks the inverse recovers m from this displayed image element.

Distinct natural numbers remain distinct when regarded as extended nonnegative reals. Every such value is finite, so adding infinity introduces no identifications among natural numbers. Lean’s characteristic-zero condition here means injectivity of the natural-number map; it does not require a field, additive inverses, or an embedding of all signed integers. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L137).

Extended nonnegative reals form a commutative monoid under addition: sums are associative and commutative, with zero as identity. Finite values add ordinarily, while any sum involving infinity is infinity. This does not supply additive inverses or unrestricted cancellation; for example, 1+∞ and 2+∞ are equal despite 1 and 2 being distinct. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L160).

Addition and multiplication of extended nonnegative reals preserve non-strict inequalities, and zero is at most one. Despite its name, Lean’s IsOrderedRing condition applies here to a semiring and supplies no additive inverses. These are weak order laws: multiplying unequal positive values by infinity can make them equal, while zero times infinity is zero. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L146).

Infinity is the greatest extended nonnegative real: every value is at most infinity. Each finite nonnegative real lies strictly below it, so infinity is an added endpoint rather than a large finite number. The order-top structure records this greatest-element property; it does not itself assert completeness or any arithmetic law. Compared with [Faris §§2.6,5.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L133).

Adding the same extended nonnegative value to two ordered values preserves their non-strict inequality, on either side. The common summand may be infinity: then both sums become infinity and the inequality remains true. This order compatibility does not promise reflection or strict preservation, which would fail for an infinite common summand. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L166).

Multiplying an inequality of extended nonnegative reals by the same value preserves non-strict order. This includes multiplication by zero or infinity, with zero times infinity defined as zero. The statement is only monotonicity: it does not allow cancelling an arbitrary nonzero multiplier, since multiplying 1 and 2 by infinity gives the same result. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L183).

Extended nonnegative reals have a linear order: any two values are comparable, and mutual comparison forces equality. Finite values are compared by their usual real order, with infinity above every finite value. This instance supplies the order structure; completeness and density are separate properties, and noncomputability does not promise an algorithm for comparing arbitrary real inputs. Compared with [Faris §§2.6,5.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L163).

The order is determined by nonnegative addition: a≤b exactly when b=a+c for some extended nonnegative c. Finite differences provide c when both values are finite, and infinity supplies it when only b is infinite. The increment need not be unique: when a=b=∞, every c works because infinity absorbs addition. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L149).

Zero is the least extended nonnegative real, so every value, including infinity, is at least zero. This is the bottom endpoint of [0,∞], not negative infinity. The order-bottom structure merely provides that least-element property; it does not turn subtraction into signed subtraction or introduce negative values into the domain. Compared with [Faris §§2.6,5.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L131).

Extended nonnegative reals combine ordered commutative addition with a greatest element infinity, which absorbs addition. This structure also requires cancellation of any finite common summand: a+b=a+c implies b=c when a≠∞. It deliberately excludes cancellation at infinity, where every sum is infinity, and it does not require negative values or additive inverses. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L173).

A product of two extended nonnegative reals can be zero only if at least one factor is zero. This remains compatible with 0·∞=0, because that product already has a zero factor. The absence of zero divisors does not imply cancellation here: 1·∞=2·∞ although the finite factors differ. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L152).

The extended nonnegative reals contain distinct elements; for example, zero and infinity are unequal. Lean’s Nontrivial condition asserts the existence of at least two values, rather than saying that every value is nonzero. It is inherited from the construction adjoining infinity to the nonnegative reals and is consistent with all the stated endpoint conventions. Compared with [Faris §§2.6,5.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L128).

Zero is the only extended nonnegative real with an additive inverse within the same domain. If a+b=0 and both values are nonnegative, then a=b=0; infinity cannot occur in such a sum. Here Lean’s AddUnits means additively invertible elements, not nonzero elements invertible under multiplication, so the word “units” needs that distinction. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L186).

An existing action of extended nonnegative scalars on any set can be restricted to finite nonnegative scalars: c acts through its inclusion into [0,∞]. This declaration supplies the restricted scalar operation. It assumes an existing action but requires no addition on the set, so the construction is more general than scalar multiplication on vector spaces. Compared with [Faris §6.2 p70](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Action.lean#L30).

A semiring carrying an algebra structure over extended nonnegative reals carries one over finite nonnegative reals. The scalar map is composed with the finite inclusion, preserving its multiplication and addition and its central image. This is restriction of scalars for semiring algebras; neither a field of scalars nor additive inverses in the algebra are required. Compared with [Faris §6.2 p70](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Action.lean#L63).

Restricting an existing action of extended nonnegative reals to finite nonnegative scalars preserves the action laws: 1·x=x and (cd)·x=c·(d·x). The acted-on set is arbitrary and need not have addition or a zero. The construction uses the multiplicative finite inclusion; it makes no additional claim that zero acts as an absorbing value. Compared with [Faris §6.2 p70](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Action.lean#L34).

A finite nonnegative scalar c acting on the extended value one produces c, regarded as an extended nonnegative real. Here the action on [0,∞] is ordinary multiplication after the finite inclusion, so this is c·1=c. Zero is allowed, and the scalar itself cannot be infinity because its type contains only finite values. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Action.lean#L41).

For any existing extended-nonnegative-scalar action, the restricted action by a finite scalar c is exactly the original action by its extended inclusion. The equality concerns the two descriptions of the same operation on an arbitrary set. It assumes an action already exists; it does not construct scalar multiplication on every set without that hypothesis. Compared with [Faris §6.2 p70](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Action.lean#L37).

Subtraction gives the least nonnegative remainder: a−b≤c exactly when a≤c+b. For finite inputs this is max(a−b,0), using ordinary real subtraction inside the maximum. The endpoint rules are ∞−finite=∞ and a−∞=0, including ∞−∞=0. These are truncated-subtraction conventions, not the partially defined signed subtraction of classical extended reals. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L171).

Between any two distinct ordered extended nonnegative reals a<b there is another value strictly between them. This includes b=∞: a must then be finite, and a larger finite value lies below infinity. The density assertion concerns intervals with distinct endpoints; it does not demand an element below zero or above infinity. Compared with [Faris §§2.6,5.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L158).

For a smooth bundle connection ∇ and smooth section s on a finite-dimensional Hausdorff manifold, ∇²s(u,v)−∇²s(v,u)=R(u,v)s. The finite-rank real bundle need not be metric. Here ∇²s(X,Y)=∇_X∇_Ys−∇_{D_XY}s uses a separate torsion-free tangent connection D, and R(X,Y)=∇_X∇_Y−∇_Y∇_X−∇_[X,Y]. Smoothness excludes the definition’s nonsmooth zero branch. See [Terek, The Ricci Identity, §2, equations(2.2),(2.7)–(2.9)](https://math-terek.github.io/texts/ricci_identity.pdf). Native Checks pass: [The general formula has the negative torsion correction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/VectorBundle/CovariantDerivative/Curvature/SecondCovariantDerivative.lean#L71), [Flat curvature gives symmetry](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/VectorBundle/CovariantDerivative/Curvature/SecondCovariantDerivative.lean#L100).
The general formula has the negative torsion correction
Flat curvature gives symmetry

On a smooth Riemannian n-manifold, connected when nonempty, a smooth metric-compatible torsion-free connection satisfying Ric=a·g has constant a when n≠0,2. Smoothness of a follows from a=Scal/n. Dimension one is included, with Ric=0; the empty manifold is harmless. The proof’s n−2 is real subtraction, so it does not truncate at zero. See [Lang, Riemannian Geometry, Proposition2.12 and Theorem2.13(1), p.28](https://metaphor.ethz.ch/x/2020/fs/401-3532-08L/sc/DG2_16June2020.pdf). Native Checks pass: [Tracing Ric=a·g gives Scal=n·a](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/VectorBundle/CovariantDerivative/Curvature/Scalar.lean#L149), [Scalar curvature is smooth](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/VectorBundle/CovariantDerivative/Curvature/Scalar.lean#L98), [Ricci curvature vanishes in dimension at most one](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/VectorBundle/CovariantDerivative/Curvature/Ricci.lean#L138).
